headline: The Construction Safety Foundation
threshold: By Lesson 10, you can greet a crew, give times and measurements, describe site conditions, ask simple questions, make polite requests and ask for help in Spanish, and start Construction Safety Lesson 1.

lessons.title: Sounds and Greetings
lessons.objective: Greet the crew, say your name and role, and pronounce basic gear words clearly.
lessons.focus: The five vowels, ch, j, ll, rr and the written accent; greetings on site

words.note: Spanish vowels are short and pure: CAS-co.
gua sounds like 'gwa': GWAN-tes.
ch sounds like the ch in 'church': cha-LE-co.
b between vowels is soft, lips barely touch.
rr is a rolled r; ll sounds like English y: ca-rre-TI-ya.
ll sounds like English y: mar-TI-yo.
j sounds like a strong English h: O-hos.
The written accent marks the stressed syllable: ca-MIÓN.

words.en: My name is Ana and I'm the safety supervisor.
words.es: Me llamo Ana y soy la supervisora de seguridad.
words.note: A man says el supervisor de seguridad.
Formal; use it with workers you don't know well.

words.en: How do you say "hard hat" in Spanish?

lessons.speaking: Greet a crew member, say your name and role, and ask how to say a piece of gear like the hard hat or vest in Spanish.

lessons.title: Numbers, Time and Measurements
lessons.objective: Say numbers, shift times and simple feet, inches, pounds and gallons on the job site.
lessons.focus: Numbers 0 to 1,000, clock time with a las, and feet, inches, pounds and gallons

words.note: Plural pies: 10 pies y 6 pulgadas. Also the foot on your body.
Common word in Mexico and the US.

words.en: The break is at half past 10.
words.es: El descanso es a las 10 y media.

words.en: There are 12 of us on the crew today.

words.es: La pared mide 10 pies y 6 pulgadas.

lessons.speaking: Tell a crew member what time the shift starts, when the break and lunch are, and how much a bucket weighs.

lessons.title: Ser and Estar
lessons.objective: Say who someone is and describe the condition and location of things on site.
lessons.focus: ser for who or what something is, estar for its condition or location on site

words.note: Feminine noun that takes el: el área está limpia.
A woman is la electricista.
estar: a condition that can change.
ser: who someone is.

words.en: The gloves are in the truck.
words.es: Los guantes están en la troca.
words.note: troca = pickup truck, common in US Spanish; estar for location.

words.es: El área de trabajo está sucia.

lessons.speaking: Walk the site with a worker and say what is broken, open, closed or dirty, who the electrician is, and where the gloves are.

lessons.title: Have, There Is, Need and Want
lessons.objective: Say what you have, what there is, what you need and what everyone has to wear.
lessons.focus: tener, hay, necesitar, querer, and hay que + infinitive for site rules

words.note: Feminine noun that takes el: el agua fría.

words.en: Do you have your safety glasses?
There's cold water in the shade.
words.es: Hay agua fría en la sombra.

words.en: I need a fire extinguisher here.
You have to wear a hard hat on the site.
words.es: Hay que usar el casco en la obra.
words.note: hay que + infinitive: a rule for everyone.

lessons.speaking: Ask a worker if they have safety glasses and earplugs, say what you need, and remind them what everyone has to wear on site.

lessons.title: Go, Do and Can
lessons.objective: Say where you are going, what the crew is going to do, and what someone can do.
lessons.focus: ir, ir a + infinitive for plans, hacer for tasks, poder for ability

words.note: Common on Mexican and US job sites; also la reunión.

words.en: I'm going to the office now.
Tomorrow we're going to work on the roof.
words.es: Mañana vamos a trabajar en el techo.
words.note: ir a + infinitive: a plan.

words.en: Today we do the cleanup at 3.
words.es: Hoy hacemos la limpieza a las 3.

words.en: You all can work on the second floor.
words.es: Ustedes pueden trabajar en el segundo piso.

words.en: The meeting is going to be at the entrance.
words.es: La junta va a ser en la entrada.
words.note: Events take ser for place: la junta es en...

lessons.speaking: Tell a crew member where you are going now, where the meeting is, and what the crew is going to do tomorrow.

lessons.title: Present Tense
lessons.objective: Talk about daily site tasks in the present tense with yo, tú, usted, nosotros and ellos.
lessons.focus: Present tense -ar, -er, -ir endings for yo, tú, usted, nosotros and ellos

words.note: Pen in Mexico and the US; elsewhere el bolígrafo.
A woman is la compañera. Coworkers usually use tú.

words.en: I check the equipment every morning.
words.es: Yo reviso el equipo cada mañana.

words.note: Informal, between coworkers.
usted takes the same verb form as él and ella.

words.es: Ellos aprenden las reglas de la obra.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker what you check each morning, who they work with today, and what the crew reads before starting work.

lessons.title: Questions
lessons.objective: Ask who, what, where, when, how many and why on the job site.
lessons.focus: Question words qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cuánto, cómo, por qué, cuál

words.note: Agrees with the noun: cuántos trabajadores, cuánta agua.
Two words in questions; porque (one word) means because.
A woman is la encargada.
Formal; to a coworker say ¿Cómo te llamas?

words.en: What time does the shift end?
How many workers are on the roof?

lessons.speaking: Ask a new worker their name, who is in charge, where the ladder is and what time the shift ends.

lessons.title: No, Never and How Much
lessons.objective: Give clear negative rules on site and ask for more, less or another item.
lessons.focus: no, nunca, nadie, nada, todavía no, más, menos and otro

words.note: Never put un before otro: otro casco.

words.en: Nobody goes in without a hard hat.

words.es: No toquen nada antes de preguntar.
words.note: Ustedes command to the whole crew.

words.en: We need more water and another first-aid kit.
words.es: Necesitamos más agua y otro botiquín.

words.en: There's less noise in the afternoon.
words.es: Hay menos ruido en la tarde.

lessons.speaking: Tell the crew that nobody goes in without a hard hat and nothing gets touched before asking, then say what you need more of.

lessons.title: Polite Requests and Commands
lessons.objective: Make polite requests and give simple usted commands to one worker.
lessons.focus: ¿Puede…? requests and usted commands like póngase, llame, espere

words.note: The two-way radio is el radio in Mexico and the US.
A woman is la supervisora.

words.en: Can you close the door, please?
Put on your hard hat, please.
words.note: Usted command; to the whole crew say pónganse.
Personal a before a person: al supervisor.

words.en: Can you hand me the radio?
Sweep the floor with the broom.
words.es: Barra el piso con la escoba.

lessons.speaking: Ask one worker politely to close the door and put on a hard hat, then tell them to call the supervisor.

lessons.title: Words You Already Know and Getting Help
lessons.objective: Recognize safety cognates and ask for help or repetition when you don't understand.
lessons.focus: Cognates ending in -ción, -dad and -ente, plus survival phrases for help

words.note: Means both safety and security; -dad words are feminine.
-ción words are feminine and match English -tion.
-ente words often match English -ent.

words.es: No entiendo; más despacio, por favor.

words.en: Can you repeat that for me?

words.note: Ustedes command to everyone nearby.

words.en: Is there anyone who speaks English?
There was an accident on the second floor.
words.es: Hubo un accidente en el segundo piso.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker you don't understand and ask them to repeat, then say there is an emergency and ask someone to call 911.
